result.text: A guest enters the restaurant when feeling hungry.
He chooses a dish from the changing meal range and waits until it is his turn.
Following this he places his order with the employee.
The employee enters the order into the POS system and collects the money from the guest.
After the payment, the employee sets up a buzzer and passes it on to the guest with the following information: "When the buzzer rings, your dinner is ready".
Afterwards the employee informs the chef of the new meal order.
The chef prepares the meal and places it in the service hatch.
He then informs the employee that he has placed the finished meal in the service hatch.
As soon as the employee is aware that the meal is ready he sets off the guest's buzzer.
This is how the guest finds out that his meal is ready for collection.
He can pick up his meal and eat it.
As soon as the guest appears at the service hatch, the employee hands over his meal.
Should a guest not react to the buzzer, the employee calls for him after 5 minutes, if necessary several times in a row.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.

result.rule: When the description says that a participant performs an action to confirm or verify that an outcome occurred: Model the confirmation as an activity; use a catch event only when the description says the process waits for a message, signal, time, or condition.

When the description says that an actor performs an action that initiates the process: Model the process trigger with an appropriate start event, then model the described action as an activity after that event; do not use the start event as a substitute for the action.

When the description says an activity continues during a defined period and that a later evaluation occurs after that period ends: Model the period end as a catching time event. If the evaluation must wait for both the period to end and the ongoing activity to finish, synchronize those paths with a parallel gateway before the evaluation.

When the description specifies what activity or process end follows an activity, a decision outcome, or a catching event, or describes waiting for alternative events: Model each described transition with a sequence flow to its stated next activity or process end. For an event-based gateway, connect each branch first to the corresponding catching event, then continue that path to its described follow-up.
